source: Nitarach (2026) Model Capability Dominates: Inference-Time Optimization Lessons from AIMO 3
finding: Gap 1. Giving different structured prompts to the majority-vote attempts of one model did not beat plain high-temperature sampling. Measured error correlation was already slightly negative, so there was nothing left to decorrelate.
numbers: gpt-oss-120b, N=8 attempts, 50 IMO-level problems, 13 baseline runs mean 39.7/50 (sd 1.7), per-attempt p about 0.69. Prompt mixes scored 36-40 (best +0.3, equal mix -1.7, 8x Classify -3.7). Pairwise error correlation: 8 points all negative, mean -0.258; N>=7 points -0.167 to -0.067.
quote: High-temperature sampling already decorrelates errors sufficiently
limits: Single model family, one benchmark, leaderboard scores with run noise of about 1.7; N=3 correlation of -0.5 is a mathematical floor; preprint, one author.
agent_relevance: Prompt diversity is not free: if sampling temperature already makes errors near-independent, weaker alt prompts cost more accuracy than they save. Measure correlation before adding frames.

source: Upravitelev et al. (2026) Multiperspectivity as a Resource for Narrative Similarity Prediction (SemEval-2026 Task 4)
finding: Gap 1. 31 personas voting on one task gave a large ensemble gain; practitioner-style personas had less correlated errors and larger gains than lay personas, at similar individual accuracy.
numbers: Pairwise error correlation r=0.388 (practitioner personas) vs 0.461 (lay), about 19% lower. Ensemble gain over mean individual: +5.0 vs +3.6 points. Single-persona ensemble 66.0 vs 75.2 at 31 personas. Test accuracy 0.705 (13th of 47). Sampling consistency predicted accuracy at item level r=+0.53; verbalised confidence r=+0.10.
quote: Accuracy improves with ensemble size, consistent with Condorcet Jury Theorem-like dynamics under weakened independence.
limits: No plain same-prompt sampling baseline and no token count, so the gain cannot be assigned to persona diversity vs just more votes. Binary choice task, 3 small models.
agent_relevance: Persona frames lower error correlation in a binary task but equal-token advantage over temperature sampling is unproven. Consistency fraction is a better truth signal than verbal confidence here.

source: Wang et al. (2025/2026, ICML) On the Effect of Sampling Diversity in Scaling LLM Inference
finding: Gap 1 and 2. Perturbing the prompt (role, instruction, injected idea, rephrasing) raised pass@100 and best-of-N, but gave no consistent gain under majority voting.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini, 100 solutions per method. Relative gains: +10.8% EM@100 MMLU-Pro, +9.6% MATH, +9.5% Pass@100 MBPP (0.8212 to 0.8992 with Instruction), +4.7% HumanEval. Irrelevant-text control (Jabberwocky) 0.8161, no gain. Proposition 5.1: vote accuracy tends to 1 only if the correct answer is the single most likely response.
limits: Mostly one model and one temperature; gains need a good verifier or judge; theory rests on two stated hypotheses. I read about the first 100k characters of the page.
agent_relevance: Diversity helps when something can pick the right sample (verifier); with plain voting it does not. Supports pairing frame diversity with a selector, not a vote.

source: Chen (2026) When Does Combining Language Models Help? A Co-Failure Ceiling on Routing, Voting, and Mixture-of-Agents Across 67 Frontier Models
finding: Gaps 3, 4, 10. Any method that outputs one member's answer (vote, router, cascade) cannot exceed 1 minus the rate where every model is wrong. Average pairwise correlation does not identify that rate. Naive voting over 3 models lost to the best single model.
numbers: 67 models, 21 providers. MATH-500: best single 0.836, oracle 0.948, beta=0.052. GPQA-Diamond (52 models): 0.846 vs oracle 1.000. code_contests (18): 0.825 vs 0.921. Learned router 0.906 vs 0.901 (CI spans zero). Mean pairwise rho 0.464 (saturated mix), 0.382 MMLU-Pro; within-family 0.528 vs cross-family 0.459. Triplet majority vote mean gain -0.10 (harder pool), -0.02 (saturated). Copula underprices all-wrong tail about 2.5x. At matched quality a heterogeneous ensemble beat Self-MoA by +0.027 at k=3 (one regime). Cascade beat random mixing by +0.114.
quote: the gains come from models that fail on different questions rather than from adding more of them.
limits: Verifiable tasks only; all-wrong counts tiny (k=17 MATH-500, k=5 code); preprint by one author; diversity result from one provider-matched band.
agent_relevance: The all-wrong rate (co-failure) is the real cap on a vote. Measure beta on our own item set, not only rho. Mixing only pays at matched quality.

source: Bertalanic and Fortuna (2026) The Cost of Consensus: Isolated Self-Correction Prevails Over Unguided Homogeneous Multi-Agent Debate
finding: Gap 7. Showing peers' answers and reasoning to a revising agent hurt versus blind self-revision. Agents copied the majority, and random unrelated rationales did as well as peer rationales.
numbers: 10 identical agents x 3 rounds; Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Ministral-3-8B; GSM-Hard (Qwen n=1017, others n=100) and MMLU-Hard. Round-3 debate vs isolated self-correction: Qwen GSM 58.8 vs 61.0; Ministral GSM 20.7 vs 48.3 (p<0.001); Qwen MMLU-Hard 60.7 vs 66.7 (p<0.001). Noise control beat debate for Qwen GSM (63.2 vs 58.8). Debate used 2.1-3.4x the tokens. Modal sycophancy 85.5%; consensus 90.1%; oracle gap 32.3 pp (Ministral GSM). Single agent with 10x output budget matched or beat debate (+6.0 pp Qwen MMLU-Hard).
quote: isolated self-correction consistently offers a more favorable cost-accuracy tradeoff
limits: Only 7-8B instruct models, N=10, one prompt; 100-item subsets carry about +-9.8% margin; peers shown in confidence order (confound); Llama differences not significant.
agent_relevance: Revision should be blind. Do not show a later step earlier sample answers; that is social influence and it damages the vote.

source: Chuang et al. (2025) Probing LLM World Models: Enhancing Guesstimation with Wisdom of Crowds Decoding
finding: Gaps 6 and 8. For numeric estimates, taking the median of 30 sampled reasoning paths beat greedy, self-consistency (mode) and the mean. The mean was ruined by outliers. Median of 5 samples beat self-consistency with 30 on two sets.
numbers: 30 CoT samples at T=1.0, 10 models, MARBLES 15 questions, FUTURE 15 post-cutoff questions, ELECPRED 51 questions. Normalised error (WOC/SC/mean/greedy), MARBLES: LLaMA-3.1-70B 0.49/1.07/3.12/6.55; Mixtral-8x22B 1.33/33.66/55.73/4.79; GPT-4-preview 1.00/1.07/1.29/1.04; human crowd 0.57/0.61/0.91 (230 people). Wilcoxon p 0.001-0.02.
quote: WOC is consistently the best decoding method.
limits: Small question sets; US-centric (weaker on German election); mechanism unexplained; Democratic-leaning bias in ELECPRED; contamination risk for later-cutoff models; no systematic prompt-variation test, so crowd-within spacing is not tested.
agent_relevance: For numeric answers use the median of samples, not the mean or the mode. Five samples may be enough. Same-prompt sampling is what was tested; reframed vs same-prompt remains open.

source: Maryanskyy, Budnikov and Kaliyev (2026) When Agents Disagree: The Selection Bottleneck in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
finding: Gaps 2 and 4. Diverse candidate pools help only if a good selector picks among them. With a judge selecting, a diverse team won 0.810 against one model; the same team with majority vote tied (0.496); synthesis lost (0.179). A homogeneous team with the same judge was at parity (0.512).
numbers: 42 tasks, 7 categories, 210 runs. Win rate vs single Opus (0.5 = parity), Bradley-Terry corrected: diverse+judge 0.810 (CI 0.768-0.851); diverse+vote 0.496; diverse+synthesis 0.179; homogeneous+judge 0.512; diverse mixed with Haiku+judge 0.929 (exploratory). Diversity effect +0.298 under judge selection. Independent re-judging cut win rates 53-67% but kept ranking (Spearman 0.90).
quote: the value of variance in the candidate pool depends entirely on the mechanism that exploits it.
limits: Judges partly circular (same judges select and score); subjective tasks, no humans; one pipeline; one temperature 0.7; weak-model result not pre-registered.
agent_relevance: On items with no verifier, spend tokens on a selector (judge from a different frame), not on more votes or on synthesis.

source: Shu (2026) When Verifiers Vote Backwards under Verdict Substitution: Signed Pivotal Value in Correlated Self-Consistency
finding: Gap 2. Replacing one of 7 votes with a separate verifier's verdict only changes the result on pivotal items (3 or 4 of 7 correct). A strong independent verifier gained a lot there; a same-source extra sample gained nothing; a weak verifier hurt. No independence assumption needed for the maths.
numbers: k=7, gpt-4o-mini T=0.8, 190 MATH-500 L4/5 problems x3 (n=570). Pivotal gain +24.2 pp (CI 14.1-33.7) with DeepSeek-V4-Flash verifier (86.4% accurate on pivotal items) vs 0.0 pp for same-source draw (65.4% to 44.1%). Role-reversed -11.2 pp (CI -20.9 to -1.2). LiveCodeBench weak verifier -24.5 pp (14 pivotal rows); strong verifier +17.5 pp. Majority-of-7 and of-17 same-source: 64.0 and 63.9 vs single call 64.1.
quote: The results therefore establish harmful verdict substitution, not universally harmful deployed plurality.
limits: Single k, one temperature; code results small-n; exploratory family not multiplicity adjusted; not a general claim that plurality is harmful.
agent_relevance: A same-model extra vote is worth about zero when votes are correlated; a differently-built verifier is worth a lot only if it is better than the voters on contested items. Gate verification on pivotal splits (3-4 of 7).

source: Fadnavis, Kanakaraj and Wyss (2026) Beyond Consensus: Trace-Level Synthesis in Mixture of Agents
finding: Gaps 1 and 2. One model, question rephrasings as the frame, same proposals: a synthesis step reading the reasoning traces beat plain voting at roughly equal call count.
numbers: gpt-oss-120b greedy; N=5 rephrasings x k=2 (11 calls) vs SC k=10 (10 calls). SC vs synthesis: BBH-3 80.4 vs 86.5; MMLU-ML 90.2 vs 92.0; GPQA-Diamond 70.7 vs 73.2; AIME 85.6 vs 91.1; LCB-Hard 57.3 vs 62.6. Beneficial vs harmful flips: 81 vs 4 across BBH, GPQA, AIME.
quote: The unit of aggregation should be the reasoning trace, not the answer.
limits: Calls are equalised but token cost is in an appendix not read; one model; several comparisons not significant (GPQA, LCB); code clustering unfaithful; contrasts with d07 where synthesis lost.
agent_relevance: Rephrased frames plus a synthesiser that reads traces can beat a vote. But d07 found synthesis worse than judge selection, so the result depends on the aggregator and model.

source: Kaniovski and Zaigraev (2009) Optimal Jury Design for Homogeneous Juries with Correlated Votes
finding: Gap 10. For equal-competence voters with equal pairwise correlation, there is a voting quota where correlation does not matter. Under simple majority, more positive correlation lowers the chance of a correct verdict. A correlated jury can do worse than one juror.
numbers: Abstract-level results: below the correlation-robust quota correlation lowers accuracy; above it, raises it; jury may be less competent than a single juror under simple majority; always worse than a single juror under unanimity.
limits: Homogeneous jury, binary choice, Bahadur representation; I read the abstract and introduction, not every proof.
agent_relevance: Majority is not the right rule when votes are correlated. A higher quota is more robust, which links to stopping and escalation rules (agreement threshold).

source: Own calculation (2026-10-31), beta-binomial model of exchangeable correlated votes (Ladha-style ceiling); script D:/research_scratch/A17.01/tmp/ladha_A17.01.py
finding: Gap 10. Given per-vote accuracy p and pairwise error correlation rho, majority accuracy of n votes and its n-to-infinity ceiling can be computed. Ceiling is P(Beta(a,b)>0.5) with a+b=(1-rho)/rho.
limits: Our own calculation, not a measurement. Assumes exchangeable votes and one shared rho; real items differ in difficulty (d04 shows all-wrong tail about 2.5x heavier than a copula). Ceiling values at rho 0.5 were numerically unreliable and are not quoted. Binary vote framing; multi-answer plurality can do better when wrong answers scatter.
agent_relevance: Rule of thumb: with rho 0.1 about 20 votes get most of the gain, and 100 votes add little. Estimate rho on our samples to set k.

source: Li, Lin, Xia and Jin (2025) Rethinking Mixture-of-Agents: Is Mixing Different Large Language Models Beneficial? (full text)
finding: Gap 4. Output quality matters more than diversity in a regression across mixtures, and mixing helps only when the members are about equal in quality.
numbers: Regression t = a*q + b*d: MMLU a=2.558 b=1.841 R2=0.771; CRUX a=4.548 b=1.421 R2=0.685; MATH a=4.719 b=2.839 R2=0.760. AlpacaEval 2.0 LC: Self-MoA 65.7 vs Mixed 59.1 (+6.6), best single 53.1. Task average 63.81 vs 60.04 (+3.8). Mixed-MoA slightly ahead only when members were similar (60.04 vs 59.69). Sequential: adding Llama-3.1-8B after 30 Qwen samples +2%; adding DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite -1.5%.
quote: MoA is quite sensitive to variations in quality
limits: Aggregator is an LLM, not a vote; small 7-9B models; the quality gap threshold is not stated as a number.
agent_relevance: Add a different role or model only if it is not clearly weaker. Diversity coefficient is positive, so diversity at equal quality helps.

source: Taubenfeld et al. (2025) Confidence Improves Self-Consistency in LLMs (CISC)
finding: Gap 5. Weighting votes by the model's own confidence saves samples. The best-calibrated confidence was the least useful; the ability to rank correct above incorrect answers for the same question mattered.
numbers: 9 open models, GSM8K, MATH, MMLU-Pro, BBH. Cost reduction at budget 5/10: P(True) 41%/46%, response probability 22%/31%, verbal 0-100 22%/30%, verbal binary 18%/10%. Accuracy gain at budget 5/10: P(True) +1.6/+1.1 pts. Within-question discrimination: P(True) 62.3%, resp. prob. 59.0%, verbal 0-100 56.1%, verbal binary 52.2% (50% is chance).
quote: the most calibrated confidence method is actually the least useful for CISC
limits: Gains are small in accuracy; all items have checkable answers; open 2B-123B models; contrasts with Denisov-Blanch (confidence weighting fails).
agent_relevance: Confidence is a weak truth signal (52-62% pair discrimination) but can cut votes about 40%. Use as a stopping aid, not as an accuracy booster.

source: Aggarwal, Madaan, Yang and Mausam (2023) Lets Sample Step by Step: Adaptive-Consistency
finding: Gap 5. A stopping rule based on the answer distribution seen so far cuts the number of samples a lot with almost no loss.
numbers: 17 reasoning and code datasets, 3 LLMs. Sample budget cut up to 7.9x, average accuracy drop below 0.1%.
limits: Abstract page only; verifiable tasks; the stopping rule assumes the leading answer is correct, so it saves cost but does not fix shared errors.
agent_relevance: Agreement fraction is a usable stopping signal for easy items. It cannot tell a shared error from a shared truth.

source: Snell, Lee, Xu and Kumar (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
finding: Gap 2. At a fixed compute budget, the best use depends on prompt difficulty: verifier search vs sequential revision. Adaptive allocation beat best-of-N by more than 4x in efficiency.
numbers: Efficiency gain over best-of-N more than 4x; on problems with non-trivial success a small model with test-time compute beat a 14x larger model at matched FLOPs.
limits: Abstract page only; uses a trained process reward model (a verifier), so it does not cover items with no verifier.
agent_relevance: Closest equal-compute head-to-head for search against a verifier vs revise; says allocation should depend on item difficulty.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
finding: Gap 2. Coverage (any sample correct) rises over four orders of magnitude of samples, but where no checker exists, majority voting and reward models plateau after several hundred samples.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite with DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct: 15.9% at 1 sample to 56% at 250 samples (single-sample state of the art 43%).
limits: Abstract page only; coverage is an upper bound that needs a verifier to realise.
agent_relevance: The gap between coverage and vote accuracy is the price of having no verifier; a checker is the best use of extra tokens when one exists.
